confidence: structural (delta signature matches the quoted rule); NOT a full end-to-end reproduction - see limitations

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.note: data/worklists/issues-c-task.md was present in the export but deliberately NOT opened: it is the C-series task spec and reading it would destroy independence.

sources_quoted.text: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.
sources_quoted.reading: The amplifier is (a) 12%, (b) restricted to MAGIC damage, (c) gated on a 700-unit range from the Abyssal holder, (d) roster-wide in its beneficiaries ("from all sources").

sources_quoted.text: {{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.
sources_quoted.reading: A 7% amplifier with NO damage-type restriction (all sources, all types), gated on an immobilize and a 4 s window.
Independent confirmation of the two constants 700 (units) and 12 (percent). No third constant exists for this passive, so no alternative amp magnitude is available in the cache.

sources_quoted.text: Imperial Mandate stats: abilityPower 60, abilityHaste 15; passives Control (20 AH vs immobilize) and Command (Vulnerable). No damage atom.
sources_quoted.reading: The cached Imperial Mandate has NO bonus-damage component at all - it is purely a 7% damage-taken amplifier. Any flat 'Mandate proc damage' row would be an unsourced literal (CLAUDE.md rule 5) and is ruled out as an explanation of the delta only insofar as the delta's size is tested below.

sources_quoted.text: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R); post = raw * m(R). Mitigation is linear in raw damage for fixed R, so a damage-taken amplifier is a pure scalar on the post-mitigation total.
sources_quoted.reading: Justifies treating both amplifiers as exact scalar multipliers on the participant's post-mitigation damage, which is what makes the ratio test below valid.

step_1_exclude_the_7_percent_amplifier.claim: The change cannot be a full withdrawal (or a full addition) of Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable amp.
step_1_exclude_the_7_percent_amplifier.math: Removing a 7% multiplicative amp can lower a total by at most 0.07/1.07 = 6.5421%. Observed drop is 6.8051% > 6.5421%.
step_1_exclude_the_7_percent_amplifier.conclusion: Some part of the 12% Unmake curse must be involved.

step_2_exclude_a_full_withdrawal_of_the_.claim: The curse was not removed from ALL of this participant's damage.
step_2_exclude_a_full_withdrawal_of_the_.math: Removing a 12% amp from the whole total would drop it by 0.12/1.12 = 10.7143%; removing both amps would drop it by 0.1984/1.1984 = 16.5554%. Observed 6.8051% sits strictly between the 7%-amp ceiling and the 12%-amp figure.
step_2_exclude_a_full_withdrawal_of_the_.conclusion: Exactly one 12%-magnitude amplifier was withdrawn from a PROPER SUBSET of the participant's damage.

step_3_size_the_subset.math: delta = 0.12 * P  =>  P = 222.5 / 0.12 = 1854.17 (post-fix, un-amped damage that lost the curse) = 60.85% of the new total 3047.1. The still-amped remainder is 1192.93 = 39.15% of the new total.
step_3_size_the_subset.under_magic_only_reading: Solving 1.12*(M+N) = 3269.6 and 1.12*M + N = 3047.1 gives base M = 1065.12 (magic), N = 1854.17 (physical/true), M+N = 2919.29, magic share = 36.49%. Round-trip check: 1.12*2919.29 = 3269.6 (old, exact); 1.12*1065.12 + 1854.17 = 3047.1 (new, exact). Both published values are reproduced to the printed precision.
step_3_size_the_subset.note: The 7% Vulnerable amp, if present on this participant in both baselines, cancels out of the ratio and does not change any conclusion above.

step_4_rule_check.quoted_rule: '...causing them to receive 12% increased MAGIC damage from all sources.'
step_4_rule_check.finding: Applying Unmake's 12% to a participant's physical/true damage contradicts the cached wiki text verbatim. The old value 3269.6 is exactly what a damage-type-AGNOSTIC 12% amp produces on a base of 2919.29; the new value 3047.1 is exactly what the same amp produces when it is confined to the 1065.12 magic component. The delta is therefore the exact arithmetic signature of narrowing a formerly type-agnostic amplifier to the magic-only scope the item text mandates.
step_4_rule_check.verdict_basis: The new value is consistent with the quoted rule; the old value is only reachable by amplifying non-magic damage with a magic-only amplifier.

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: Old used a different curse constant (e.g. 20%) later corrected to 12%.
alternative_hypotheses_tested.test: (1 + 0.20 f)/(1 + 0.12 f) = 1.07302 requires f = 1.025 > 1 - impossible. Same test for a mis-valued Vulnerable amp (10% -> 7%) requires f = 2.93; (15% -> 7%) requires f = 0.975 but yields ratio 1.07477 at f = 1, never 1.07302.
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: Ruled out. The cache also contains no constant other than 12 for Unmake and 7 for Command.

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: Curse double-counted (1.12^2) on the magic portion, fixed to a single application.
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: Arithmetically possible. Direction still favours the new value (a fix).

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: Target-range gating: this breakdown entry's target sits outside Unmake's 700-unit radius, so the curse should never have applied to it; the fix range-gates the curse.
alternative_hypotheses_tested.test: Requires the whole magic component (60.85% of the new total) to lose the amp - internally consistent.
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: Arithmetically possible. Direction favours the new value (a fix), and the 700-unit gate is explicit in the quoted text.

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: REGRESSION: the change stripped the curse's roster-wide benefit, so this ally no longer gets the amp on its magic damage.
alternative_hypotheses_tested.test: Same arithmetic signature as the range-gating hypothesis (12% withdrawn from a 60.85% magic share).
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: Cannot be excluded by arithmetic alone. It IS excluded on rule grounds only if the amp is still applied to some ally: the text's 'from all sources' makes a blanket ally-stripping wrong. This is the single hypothesis under which the OLD value would be correct, and it is the minority reading.

alternative_hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: A flat removed row (e.g. a legacy Imperial Mandate bonus-damage proc worth 222.5).
alternative_hypotheses_tested.test: The cached Imperial Mandate has no damage atom and no damage numbers in any branch; any such row would have been an unsourced literal.
alternative_hypotheses_tested.result: If this were the change, the new value is still the correct one (the removed row has no source in the cache).

limitations: The golden scenario definition for 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster' (roster composition, levels, items, target resistances, which participant is breakdown[2]) lives outside the permitted evidence tree - it is not present anywhere under data/ (grep for '_roster' and 'mandate' over the whole export returns no scenario). I therefore could not re-run the fight end to end.

What I could do independently is (a) fix the governing constants and their scope from the cached wiki text, and (b) decompose the observed 222.5 delta against every amplifier the two items expose. That decomposition is decisive about the SIZE and MAGNITUDE of the amplifier that moved (a 12% amp withdrawn from 60.85% of the participant's damage) and rules out the 7% Vulnerable amp as a sufficient explanation.

Of the five structural stories that reproduce the delta exactly, four imply the new value is the corrected one and one (blanket removal of the roster-wide 'from all sources' benefit) would imply the old value was correct. The verdict follows the majority reading plus the verbatim 'increased MAGIC damage' restriction, which the old value violates under the most direct reading.
